book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: to the assembly of God which is at Corinth—those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I always thank my God concerning you for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: that in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and all knowledge—

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you—

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: so that you come behind in no gift, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I beg you, brothers, through the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfected together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are from Chloe’s household, that there are contentions among you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I mean this, that each one of you says, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” and, “I follow Christ.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: so that no one should say that I had baptized you into my own name.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: (I also baptized the household of Stephanas; besides them, I don’t know whether I baptized any other.)

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the Good News—not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ wouldn’t be made void.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. I will bring the discernment of the discerning to nothing.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Hasn’t God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For seeing that in the wisdom of God, the world through its wisdom didn’t know God, it was God’s good pleasure through the foolishness of the preaching to save those who believe.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For Jews ask for signs, Greeks seek after wisdom,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Greeks,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For you see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: but God chose the foolish things of the world that he might put to shame those who are wise. God chose the weak things of the world that he might put to shame the things that are strong.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: God chose the lowly things of the world, and the things that are despised, and the things that don’t exist, that he might bring to nothing the things that exist,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: that no flesh should boast before God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: We speak wisdom, however, among those who are full grown, yet a wisdom not of this world nor of the rulers of this world who are coming to nothing.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that has been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But as it is written, “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But to us, God revealed them through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man which is in him? Even so, no one knows the things of God except God’s Spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But we received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that were freely given to us by God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: We also speak these things, not in words which man’s wisdom teaches but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now the natural man doesn’t receive the things of God’s Spirit, for they are foolishness to him; and he can’t know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But he who is spiritual discerns all things, and he himself is to be judged by no one.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord that he should instruct him?” But we have Christ’s mind.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Brothers, I couldn’t speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I fed you with milk, not with solid food, for you weren’t yet ready. Indeed, you aren’t ready even now,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you fleshly?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed, and each as the Lord gave to him?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or straw,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: each man’s work will be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man’s work is.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If any man’s work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If any man’s work is burned, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but as through fire.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t you know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit lives in you?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which you are.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool that he may become wise.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He has taken the wise in their craftiness.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: And again, “The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come. All are yours,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So let a man think of us as Christ’s servants and stewards of God’s mysteries.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by a human court. Yes, I don’t even judge my own self.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now these things, brothers, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you might learn not to think beyond the things which are written, that none of you be puffed up against one another.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you didn’t receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: You are already filled. You have already become rich. You have come to reign without us. Yes, and I wish that you did reign, that we also might reign with you!

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I don’t write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For God’s Kingdom is not in word, but in power.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles, that one has his father’s wife.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: You are arrogant, and didn’t mourn instead, that he who had done this deed might be removed from among you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together with my spirit with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: you are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore let’s keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortionists, or with idolaters, for then you would have to leave the world.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother who is a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortionist. Don’t even eat with such a person.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For what do I have to do with also judging those who are outside? Don’t you judge those who are within?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But those who are outside, God judges. “Put away the wicked man from among yourselves.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t you know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t you know that we will judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If then you have to judge things pertaining to this life, do you set them to judge who are of no account in the assembly?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I say this to move you to shame. Isn’t there even one wise man among you who would be able to decide between his brothers?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers!

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore it is already altogether a defect in you that you have lawsuits one with another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: No, but you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and that against your brothers.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Or don’t you know that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s Kingdom? Don’t be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostitutes, nor homosexuals,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor extortionists, will inherit God’s Kingdom.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Some of you were such, but you were washed. You were sanctified. You were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: “Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods,” but God will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t you know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Or don’t you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, “The two”, he says, “will become one flesh.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let the husband give his wife the affection owed her, and likewise also the wife her husband.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The wife doesn’t have authority over her own body, but the husband does. Likewise also the husband doesn’t have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t deprive one another, unless it is by consent for a season, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer, and may be together again, that Satan doesn’t tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But this I say by way of concession, not of commandment.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Yet I wish that all men were like me. However, each man has his own gift from God, one of this kind, and another of that kind.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I say to the unmarried and to widows, it is good for them if they remain even as I am.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if they don’t have self-control, let them marry. For it’s better to marry than to burn with passion.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But to the married I command—not I, but the Lord—that the wife not leave her husband

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: (but if she departs, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not leave his wife.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But to the rest I—not the Lord—say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is content to live with her, let her not leave her husband.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us in peace.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Only, as the Lord has distributed to each man, as God has called each, so let him walk. So I command in all the assemblies.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but what matters is keeping God’s commandments.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let each man stay in that calling in which he was called.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Were you called being a bondservant? Don’t let that bother you, but if you get an opportunity to become free, use it.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For he who was called in the Lord being a bondservant is the Lord’s free man. Likewise he who was called being free is Christ’s bondservant.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: You were bought with a price. Don’t become bondservants of men.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Brothers, let each man, in whatever condition he was called, stay in that condition with God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore I think that because of the distress that is on us, it’s good for a man to remain as he is.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Are you bound to a wife? Don’t seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? Don’t seek a wife.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I say this, brothers: the time is short. From now on, both those who have wives may be as though they had none;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: and those who weep, as though they didn’t weep; and those who rejoice, as though they didn’t rejoice; and those who buy, as though they didn’t possess;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: and those who use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I desire to have you to be free from cares. He who is unmarried is concerned for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: but he who is married is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: There is also a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she who is married cares about the things of the world—how she may please her husband.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: This I say for your own benefit, not that I may ensnare you, but for that which is appropriate, and that you may attend to the Lord without distraction.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He doesn’t sin. Let them marry.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no urgency, but has power over his own will, and has determined in his own heart to keep his own virgin, does well.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So then both he who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and he who doesn’t give her in marriage does better.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: A wife is bound by law for as long as her husband lives; but if the husband is dead, she is free to be married to whomever she desires, only in the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment, and I think that I also have God’s Spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But anyone who loves God is known by him.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no other God but one.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For though there are things that are called “gods”, whether in the heavens or on earth—as there are many “gods” and many “lords”—

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: yet to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we live through him.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: However, that knowledge isn’t in all men. But some, with consciousness of an idol until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But food will not commend us to God. For neither, if we don’t eat are we the worse, nor if we eat are we the better.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if a man sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol’s temple, won’t his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: And through your knowledge, he who is weak perishes, the brother for whose sake Christ died.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Thus, sinning against the brothers, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will eat no meat forever more, that I don’t cause my brother to stumble.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Aren’t you my work in the Lord?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: My defense to those who examine me is this:

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Have we no right to eat and to drink?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Have we no right to take along a wife who is a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and doesn’t eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and doesn’t drink from the flock’s milk?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or doesn’t the law also say the same thing?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.” Is it for the oxen that God cares,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes in hope should partake of his hope.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If others partake of this right over you, don’t we yet more? Nevertheless we didn’t use this right, but we bear all things, that we may cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t you know that those who serve around sacred things eat from the things of the temple, and those who wait on the altar have their portion with the altar?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Even so the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I have used none of these things, and I don’t write these things that it may be done so in my case; for I would rather die, than that anyone should make my boasting void.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if I preach the Good News, I have nothing to boast about, for necessity is laid on me; but woe is to me if I don’t preach the Good News.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if not of my own will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What then is my reward? That when I preach the Good News, I may present the Good News of Christ without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Good News.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For though I was free from all, I brought myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: to those who are without law, as without law (not being without law toward God, but under law toward Christ), that I might win those who are without law.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I do this for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, so that you may win.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I therefore run like that, not aimlessly. I fight like that, not beating the air,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: However with most of them, God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let’s not commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let’s not test Christ, as some of them tested, and perished by the serpents.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t grumble, as some of them also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now all these things happened to them by way of example, and they were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The cup of blessing which we bless, isn’t it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, isn’t it a sharing of the body of Christ?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Because there is one loaf of bread, we, who are many, are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf of bread.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Consider Israel according to the flesh. Don’t those who eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What am I saying then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I don’t desire that you would have fellowship with demons.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: You can’t both drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You can’t both partake of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” don’t eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience. For “the earth is the Lord’s, with all its fullness.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other’s conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced for something I give thanks for?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Whether therefore you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Give no occasion for stumbling, whether to Jews, to Greeks, or to the assembly of God;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered dishonors her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaved.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if a woman is not covered, let her hair also be cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, let her be covered.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For a man indeed ought not to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: for man wasn’t created for the woman, but woman for the man.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For this cause the woman ought to have authority over her own head, because of the angels.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Nevertheless, neither is the woman independent of the man, nor the man independent of the woman, in the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For as woman came from man, so a man also comes through a woman; but all things are from God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Judge for yourselves. Is it appropriate that a woman pray to God unveiled?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Doesn’t even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given to her for a covering.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if any man seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither do God’s assemblies.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But in giving you this command I don’t praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For there also must be factions among you, that those who are approved may be revealed among you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: When therefore you assemble yourselves together, it is not the Lord’s supper that you eat.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For in your eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What, don’t you have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise God’s assembly and put them to shame who don’t have enough? What shall I tell you? Shall I praise you? In this I don’t praise you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: When he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: In the same way he also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way unworthy of the Lord will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy way eats and drinks judgment to himself if he doesn’t discern the Lord’s body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For this cause many among you are weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if we discerned ourselves, we wouldn’t be judged.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But when we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest your coming together be for judgment. The rest I will set in order whenever I come.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I don’t want you to be ignorant.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For the body is not one member, but many.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If they were all one member, where would the body be?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But now they are many members, but one body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part;

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial will be done away with.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Follow after love and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God, for no one understands, but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but even more that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Even lifeless things that make a sound, whether pipe or harp, if they didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If then I don’t know the meaning of the language, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What should I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: However, in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Brothers, don’t be children in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: In the law it is written, “By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people. They won’t even listen to me that way, says the Lord.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to those who believe.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If therefore the whole assembly is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, won’t they say that you are crazy?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, or has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If any man speaks in another language, let there be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let two or three of the prophets speak, and let the others discern.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be exhorted.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: for God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Whether then it is I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith also is in vain.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up if it is true that the dead are not raised.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Wake up righteously and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is also a spiritual body.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: So also it is written, “The first man Adam became a living soul.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now concerning the collection for the saints: as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: On the first day of every week, let each one of you save as he may prosper, that no collections are made when I come.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Let all that you do be done in love.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: Now I beg you, brothers—you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints—

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labors.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in their house.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be cursed. Come, Lord!

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

book_name: Paul’s First Letter to the Corinthians
text: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: One who says, “I know him,” and doesn’t keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth isn’t in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: But God’s love has most certainly been perfected in whoever keeps his word. This is how we know that we are in him:

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: He who says he is in the light and hates his brother is in the darkness even until now.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: But he who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, little children, because you know the Father.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: For all that is in the world—the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life—isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Little children, these are the end times, and as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen. By this we know that it is the final hour.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have continued with us. But they left, that they might be revealed that none of them belong to us.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all have knowledge.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: I have not written to you because you don’t know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Whoever denies the Son doesn’t have the Father. He who confesses the Son has the Father also.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Therefore, as for you, let that remain in you which you heard from the beginning. If that which you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son, and in the Father.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: This is the promise which he promised us, the eternal life.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: These things I have written to you concerning those who would lead you astray.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: As for you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you, and you don’t need for anyone to teach you. But as his anointing teaches you concerning all things, and is true, and is no lie, and even as it taught you, you will remain in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness and not be ashamed before him at his coming.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and no sin is in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him, and he can’t sin, because he is born of God.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil. Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: For this is the message which you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another—

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: unlike Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. Why did he kill him? Because his deeds were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Don’t be surprised, my brothers, if the world hates you.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: And by this we know that we are of the truth and persuade our hearts before him,

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Beloved, if our hearts don’t condemn us, we have boldness toward God;

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: so whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: This is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he commanded.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him. By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God,

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: and every spirit who doesn’t confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God; and this is the spirit of the Antichrist, of whom you have heard that it comes. Now it is in the world already.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: They are of the world. Therefore they speak of the world, and the world hears them.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: We are of God. He who knows God listens to us. He who is not of God doesn’t listen to us. By this we know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: We have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as the Savior of the world.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: In this, love has been made perfect among us, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment, because as he is, even so we are in this world.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: We love him, because he first loved us.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: This commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should also love his brother.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep his commandments.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood. It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.

book_name: John’s First Letter
text: For there are three who testify:

book_name: John’s First Letter
